s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of binocular horizontal diplopia with cranial nerve palsy following a procedure
salient_findings: Binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze
Inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline
key_facts: Woman in her 50s
Presented with bilateral nasal obstruction
Thick nasal discharge
Facial pain and pressure
Condition recalcitrant to 3 prior surgeries, immunotherapy, and medical therapy
Binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze
Inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline
Left eye was not proptotic, ecchymotic, or tense
Bedside intraocular pressure measurements: 15 OD, 16 OS (normal)
National Institutes of Health stroke score of 1
Workup results were negative for a cerebrovascular accident

s4.champion: Transient left abducens (cranial nerve VI) nerve palsy

raw.champion: Transient left abducens (cranial nerve VI) nerve palsy
raw.rationale: The patient presented with binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze and inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline, which are characteristic symptoms of abducens nerve palsy. The condition resolved by postoperative day 1, suggesting a transient cause.

rejected.label: Iatrogenic Abducens Nerve Palsy
rejected.why: While possible, the transient nature of the palsy suggests it may not be directly caused by a medical procedure.

rejected.label: Allergic fungal rhinosinusitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms of bilateral nasal obstruction, thick nasal discharge, and facial pain and pressure are not directly related to the abducens nerve palsy.

rejected.label: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps
rejected.why: Similar to allergic fungal rhinosinusitis, this condition does not explain the abducens nerve palsy.

rejected.label: Sphenopalatine ganglion blockade complication
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence in the vignette that the patient underwent a sphenopalatine ganglion blockade procedure.
